findings.summary: All three panels sit inside one 14.0 x 7.2 in canvas drawn at equal aspect, so each tall machine is rendered in a narrow column of the wide canvas. Measured on the delivered PNGs, plotted content occupies x 560-841 (281 px, 20.1 %) for MAST-U, x 593-796 (203 px, 14.5 %) for TCV and x 603-798 (195 px, 13.9 %) for ITER of a 1399 px width: about 80 % of the figure is empty white. The contour detail and null marks are therefore drawn at roughly a fifth of the size the canvas could give them, which is what makes the grey reference and the null markers marginal at page-column width. Folded: size the canvas width to each machine's aspect, or place the three panels side by side on one shared-scale canvas.

In the TCV panel the reference and nova contours nearly coincide, so the 2.6 pt grey imas-efit line is almost entirely covered by the 1.4 pt blue nova line drawn over it. At native resolution grey remains visible as a fringe along the outer right and lower edges, but at the ~900 px evidence column that fringe disappears and the panel reads as a single blue contour set. Exempted: the wide-reference-under-narrow-subject encoding is the documented design, so agreement reads as a narrow line centred in a wide one, and the served vector figure preserves the grey where raster downsampling loses it; the finding is recorded so a future layout or caption change can address the page-scale read.

In the ITER panel the two null-marker pairs coincide almost entirely: at the axis the blue triangle sits on the grey reference triangle, and at the X-point the blue cross sits on the grey cross, with only a sliver of the reference shade showing. At native resolution both shades are discernible; at page-column width each pair reads as one dark mark, so the figure silently drops the statement that the two states agree on the null locations. The same overlap is present but milder on MAST-U. Exempted: the overlap records a genuine coincidence of the two null estimates and both marks are distinguishable on the delivered PNG at native resolution.

In the ITER panel a fan of blue and grey contours in the lower-left terminates against the bottom-left wall corner, and several arcs stop short in the interior, with nothing on the figure or in its caption saying what that region is. The content bounding box stops at y 672 of 720, so this is not a canvas clip: the contours end where the node grid meets the wall. A reader cannot tell whether this is a private-flux or scrape-off region truncated by the grid or a solved structure the wall cut off. Exempted: the truncation faithfully renders the data boundary the fit was solved over; a caption clause naming the region would remove the ambiguity.

The three captions (lines 19-21) state which colour is which, 'both null sets' and the wall, but omit the terminal residual and the converged flag, and every state drawn is a non-converged terminal state (MAST-U misfit 50, TCV 6.978, ITER 10.03; converged 'no' on all three in the table above). The panels draw tidy closed contours under a two-entry legend, so a reader can take them for solved equilibria with no way to learn from the figure or its caption that the fit was still moving when its 96-pass budget ended. The section's plotting rule asks for the terminal residual and the converged flag in the caption. Folded: add the residual and converged flag to each caption in a follow-up fragment edit.

Neither the legend nor the captions identify the null marks: the figure shows a solid triangle at the core and cross marks near the divertor in two shades, with no statement that the triangle is the magnetic axis and the cross the admitted X-point, nor which shade belongs to which state. The legend's own two entries are drawn with triangle glyphs, so the legend reinforces the ambiguity by reusing the axis-marker shape for a series key. On ITER and MAST-U, where the two shades coincide, the marks are the only place the null comparison can be read. Folded: add one caption clause naming the marker vocabulary and the shading, and drop the triangle glyph from the legend key.

rubric_items.contrast: pass: legend text is near-black on white in all three; the grey reference colour measures about 3.1:1 against white and is distinguished from the blue by lightness as well as hue.
rubric_items.data_ink: pass: unfilled line contours, the wall outline and null marks are the only ink in every panel; no fills, gradients, gridlines, frames, ticks or value labels.
rubric_items.decoration: pass: no gradient, background fill, shading, drop shadow or styled theme in any panel; axes are off and each figure-level legend is frameless.
rubric_items.label_collision: pass: no text is clipped at a canvas edge or overlaps another text or the data in any panel (content within x 557-841, y 17-677, no ink on any edge). Overlapping null markers are data marks rather than labels and are recorded as non-blocking findings.
rubric_items.legibility: pass with recorded weaknesses: all three panels are readable at their native 1399x720 resolution — wall, both contour families and both null sets visible. The panels fill only 13.9-20.1 % of the canvas width, the TCV grey reference degrades to invisible at page-column width, and coincident null markers merge; these are recorded as non-blocking findings, not as a blocked read.
rubric_items.table_form: pass: all three are poloidal flux maps, a spatial relationship a table cannot carry; the per-case numbers are published in the table above the panels.
